L40: # Grades and records
L41: 
L42: ## ASU Transcripts
L43: 
L44: ### Official and unofficial ASU academic transcripts are available through University Registrar Services.
L45: 
L46: Sending your transcripts to ASU? 【39†Contact Admissions†admission.asu.edu】 for mailing address information.
L47: ### Official Transcripts
L48: An official transcript is a copy of the student's permanent academic record issued by the University Registrar. It displays all courses taken for credit at ASU and includes all grades received. Unlike unofficial copies, paper and electronic copies of the official transcript display the ASU seal and list a print date. The official paper copies are also signed by the registrar.  Effective July 1, 2024, official transcripts are not held for past due financial obligations to the university.
L49: 
L50: * * *
L51: For students that attended the Thunderbird School of Global Management prior to December 31, 2014, information on ordering official transcripts can be found 【40†here】.
L52: 
L53: * * *
L54: 
L55: ASU cannot send official transcripts by email or fax.
L56: 
L57: University Registrar Services has partnered with Parchment, a digital credentials service, to manage the ordering, processing, and secure electronic delivery of your official ASU transcripts.
L58: All students are encouraged to go online to place their transcript order. This is the easiest and most efficient way to place an order for either a traditional paper transcript or electronic transcript delivery.
L59: #### Electronic Delivery of Official Transcripts
L60: 
L61: Official electronic transcripts may only be ordered using Parchment’s online request system. Students choosing this option will identify their recipients by selecting them from a list within the ordering system or by providing the email address of their intended recipients.
L62: 
L63: To expedite and ensure accurate delivery, students should:
L64:   * Make sure the transcript recipient will accept the electronic transcripts, so they can avoid paying to send a replacement copy.
L65:   * Double check that the email address they provided for an institution or individual is correct, so they can avoid paying again to send a replacement electronic or paper copy.
L66:   * Provide their email addresses for notification purposes (the student’s email address assists with tracking and confirming delivery by notifying the student when the transcript is sent and when it is received by the selected institution or individual).
L67:   * Instruct recipients to allow emails from Parchment (【41†[email protected]】) to avoid potential problems with spam filters.
L68: Orders are generally processed immediately, unless you request a hold for degree or grades. (Degrees are posted approximately 6 weeks after the conferral date for the semester.)
L69: 
L70: The transcript is not delivered by email; the recipient’s email address is used for notification and reminder messages regarding delivery of the student’s transcript to a secure site where it can be accessed.
L71: #### Ordering Official Transcripts
L72: 
L73: Official transcripts can be ordered online or by mail.
L74: ##### Online
L75:   * Students who have an ASURITE ID — Sign in to 【4†My ASU†my.asu.edu】 and order official transcripts online. In the My Classes box, click Grades & Transcripts and then Transcripts & Test Scores (see sample My ASU navigation screenshot below).
L76:   * Students who attended ASU after 1980 and who do not yet have an 【42†ASURITE ID†asu.my.salesforce-sites.com】 or do not know their ASURITE ID and password — Please contact the ASU Help Desk at 855-278-5080 for assistance requesting your ASURITE ID.
L77:   * Students who attended ASU prior to 1980 and do not have an ASURITE ID — Request transcripts in person or by mail.
L78: 【43†Image: transcripts and test scores on My ASU dashboard】
L79: ##### By Mail
L80: 
L81: Students may order transcripts by submitting a 【44†Request for Official Transcript Form】 or signed letter including the following information:
L82: 
L83:   * Name
L84:   * Former names (if applicable)
L85:   * Arizona State University identification number (or SSN)
L86:   * Date of birth
L87:   * First and last dates of attendance
L88:   * Current return address
L89:   * Daytime phone number
L90:   * Specific mailing address for each transcript ordered
L91: Pre-payment is required. See costs for official transcripts below. Make check or money order payable to Arizona State University.
L92: 
L93: Send requests for official transcripts to:
L94: 
L95: Outgoing Transcripts
L96: University Registrar Services
L97: Arizona State University
L98: P.O. Box 870312
L99: Tempe, AZ 85287-0312
L100: 
L101: For further assistance, please contact Outgoing Transcripts at 480-965-7276 or 【45†[email protected]】
L102: #### In Person
L103: 
L104: Students presenting photo ID may order official transcripts in person at the Cashier's Office at the following locations:
L105:   * Downtown Phoenix campus — Mon. - Fri. 8:15 a.m. - 4:30 p.m., University Center Building, Suite 112
L106:   * Polytechnic campus — Mon. - Fri. 8:15 a.m. - 4:30 p.m., Administration Building, Room 160
L107:   * Tempe campus — Mon. - Fri. 8:15 a.m. - 4:30 p.m., Student Services Building, 244
L108:   * West campus — Mon. - Fri. 8:15 a.m. to 4:30 p.m., University Center Building, Room 101
L109: #### Costs
L110: 
L111: All charges for official transcripts must be paid at time of request. Official transcripts cost $15.00 per official transcript copy requested.
L112: Starting January 6th, 2025, sales tax will be collected in compliance with federal, state, and local tax laws. This change may affect the total cost of your request based on various factors such as document type, delivery method, and location. Before completing your order online, you will see a breakdown of all charges, including any applicable taxes, to ensure total transparency.
L113: Rush transcripts (same day service): $10.00 in addition to the costs for the total number of transcripts ordered. Available for in-person requests only.
L114:   * Special delivery in the U.S. — Special delivery processing, instead of regular mail, is available via FedEx or U.S. Express Mail at $35.00 per recipient, in addition to the costs for the total number of transcripts ordered.
L115:   * Special delivery outside the U.S. — Express delivery to addresses outside the U.S. is available through International FedEx Express or International Express Mail at $65.00 per recipient, in addition to the costs for the total number of transcripts ordered.
L116: FedEx requires a street address for delivery. FedEx charges an additional fee for all returned shipments, and the student will be responsible for paying the total amount before the transcript(s) will be mailed.
L117: 
L118: Transcripts will not be reissued after 90 days from the processed date.
L119: 
L120: Fees subject to change without notice.
L121: ##### Apostille
L122: 
L123: For 【46†information on requesting an Apostille.】
L124: ### Unofficial Transcripts
L125: 
L126: An unofficial transcript is an uncertified copy of the student's academic record. In addition to courses taken for credit at ASU and grades received, unofficial transcripts also include information such as note records regarding Dean’s List achievement, grade changes, semester GPAs and probation/disqualification status.
L127: 
L128: * * *
L129: For students that attended the Thunderbird School of Global Management prior to December 31, 2014, information on ordering unofficial transcripts can be found 【47†here】.
L130: 
L131: * * *
L132: #### Accessing and Ordering Unofficial Transcripts
L133: 
L134: Here's how to view and request unofficial transcripts:
L135: ##### Online
L136:   * Students and former students who have an ASURITE ID — 【48†Sign in to view and print an unofficial transcript†www.asu.edu】. You may need to temporarily disable pop-up blocker for this site to retrieve your transcript.
L137:   * Students who attended after 1980 and who do not have an ASURITE ID or do not know their ASURITE ID and password — Request an 【42†ASURITE ID†asu.my.salesforce-sites.com】 to access unofficial transcripts online by contacting the ASU Help Desk at 855-278-5080.
L138:   * Students who attended prior to 1980 — ASU does not offer online transcript services for students who attended prior to 1980. Request the unofficial transcript in person, by mail or by fax.
L139: You should be in your My ASU student view to access your transcripts. If you have both a student and staff view, this will be indicated in the top right of your screen.
L140: 
L141: 【49†Image: transcripts and test scores on My ASU dashboard】
L142: ##### By Mail or Fax
L143: 
L144: Students may order an unofficial transcript by mailing or faxing a signed letter including the following information about the student:
L145: 
L146:   * Name and former names (if applicable)
L147:   * Arizona State University identification number (or SSN)
L148:   * Date of birth
L149:   * First and last dates of attendance
L150:   * Current return address
L151:   * Daytime phone number
L152:   * Return Fax number or specific mailing address
L153: Requests for unofficial transcripts by mail or fax must be signed by the student. No computer generated signatures will be accepted. Please send requests for unofficial transcripts to:
L154: 
L155: Outgoing Transcripts
L156: University Registrar Services
L157: Arizona State University
L158: P.O. Box 870312
L159: Tempe, AZ 85287-0312
L160: 
L161: Fax: 602-543-8312
L162: #### In Person
L163: 
L164: Students presenting photo ID may order unofficial transcripts in person at any campus 【50†registration site】.
L165: 
L166: #### Costs
L167: 
L168: There is no fee for an unofficial transcript. For assistance, please contact 【50†University Registrar Services】.
L169: ### Transcript FAQs
L170: 
L171: Have questions? Here are the most common 【51†FAQs】.
L172: 
L173: If you have an ASURITE ID, want to order online, and are familiar with the applicable transcript policies, you can access your transcripts through 【4†My ASU†my.asu.edu】.
L174: 
L175: 【4†My ASU†my.asu.edu】
L176: 
L177: Click Grades & Transcripts in the My Classes box, then Transcripts & Test Scores.

L46: Can high school students take these courses?
L47: 
L48: Yes, any learner with an internet connection and a valid ID (or birth certificate, for learners under 18) can take these courses and earn credit, including high school students.
L49: 
L50: How do I verify my identity?
L51: Earned Admission learners are required to authenticate their identity before their course begins with a live photo and an approved form of photo identification. This includes government-issued IDs, school IDs, or birth certificates for learners under 18. Your photo ID must match the name associated with your ASU account.
L52: If you’re under the age of 18, you may provide a birth certificate to begin the course, but if your course requires proctoring, a government-issued ID is required to take the exam and complete the course.
L53: Can I get an ASU ID card after I register?
L54: 
L55: No, ASU ID cards are issued to admitted ASU students only.
L56: 
L57: Will I get an asu.edu email after I register for Universal Learner Courses?
L58: 
L59: No, ASU has transitioned away from issuing emails and supports using personal emails. ASU emails are only issued when a course requires it for the completion of the course. Most courses do not require ASU emails for completion. Learners will not retain access to ASU Gmail once they are no longer actively enrolled in ULCs.
L60: 【8†Image】
L61: ## Courses
L62: 
L63: When do I need to be online for my courses?
L64: 
L65: Earned Admission’s Universal Learner Courses are asynchronous which means they do not have any live content. While there are weekly due dates in most courses, you can complete the coursework when it is convenient for you. Some courses hold live office hours with instructors, but these are not required and the content is recorded and posted in the course to view whenever works best for you.
L66: 
L67: Do I need to order any textbooks or materials?
L68: No, you do not need to order any textbooks or materials. All materials are provided when the course opens.
L69: 
L70: How can I get academic support in my courses?
L71: 
L72: Visit the 【9†ULC Online Study Hub†tutoring.asu.edu】 for academic support. You will need to use your ASURITE to access it.
L73: 
L74: How do I access my ASU Gmail account?
L75: ASU emails are only issued when a course requires it for the completion of the course. Most courses do not require ASU emails for completion. Sign in to your 【10†My ASU†my.asu.edu】 and select the Gmail shortcut link located in your shortcuts list. If you don’t see the Gmail shortcut link select View More and select Gmail from the drop-down. You can also access your ASU Gmail by going to 【11†email.asu.edu†email.asu.edu】. If you are unable to access your Gmail, please contact 【12†[email protected]】.
L76: If I unenroll, will it appear on my transcript?
L77: 
L78: No. There is no risk to your academic record with Earned Admission and Universal Learner Courses since you don’t pay to add them to your transcript until you choose. If you find that now’s not the time for you to take a course, you can easily unenroll at any time on your learner dashboard.
L79: 
L80: What does on-demand and session-based mean?
L81: On-demand is a course you can start today that can be completed at your own pace. You must spend a minimum of 6 weeks enrolled in the course and have 1 year to complete it. Session-based is a course with a specific start date and the structure of a cohort with other learners and due dates.
L82: 
L83: Is on-demand or session-based right for me?
L84: Not all courses are available in both formats but we encourage learners to enroll in session-based courses whenever possible. We find that learners are more successful in session-based courses where they can move through the course material with other learners and have due dates for assignments. On-demand courses are best for learners who have to take long absences from internet connectivity.
L85: 
L86: How long do I have access to the course?
L87: You’ll have access to the course materials (readings, videos, presentations, etc.) for 2 weeks after the course ends for all session-based courses and on-demand courses will be closed upon request for academic credit.
L88: 
L89: How can I get enrollment verification?
L90: A letter can be written verifying your enrollment in your current Universal Learner Courses. To request a letter, please reach out to our support team at 【13†[email protected]】. This letter can only be sent directly to the learner and cannot be provided to other institutions or organizations.
L91: 
L92: Can I get my student loans deferred while taking Universal Learner Courses?
L93: No, we are unable to complete any loan-related forms. Learners enrolled in Universal Learner Courses are not considered admitted to Arizona State University. At this time, the only documentation we are able to provide is an Enrollment Verification (EV) letter.
L94: 
L95: 【14†Image】
L96: ## Payment
L97: 
L98: How much does it cost to take courses for Earned Admission?
L99: 
L100: You’ll pay a $25 course enrollment fee to reserve your place in the course. If you’d like to add the course to your ASU transcript for college credit, you’ll need to pay a fee of $400 following the completion of your course if you are satisfied with your grade.
L101: 
L102: Are there any hidden fees?
L103: No, we only have two fees associated with our courses:
L104: • $25 course enrollment fee
L105: • $400 to add it to your ASU transcript for college credit (This fee is paid at the end of the course if you are satisfied with your grade.)
L106: If you apply to ASU, you’ll also pay an application fee. Learn more about the 【5†admissions process†asuonline.asu.edu】.
L107: 
L108: Can I get financial aid?
L109: Although Earned Admission’s Universal Learner Courses aren’t eligible for federal financial aid, you can register for just $25 per course. This low cost makes higher education accessible without loans or debt. After passing your course, you have up to one year to add the credits to your ASU transcript for $400 per course. Financial aid is available once you are admitted to the university. Submit your application early to be eligible for financial aid once you meet the minimum required credits.
L110: Should I complete a FAFSA?
L111: 
L112: If you are using Universal Learner Courses to earn admission to ASU, yes. We recommend completing a FAFSA when you are nearing the end of your Earned Admission courses, before you are admitted to ASU. Learn more about submitting your Free Application for Federal Student Aid (FAFSA) 【15†here†asuonline.asu.edu】.
L113: 
L114: I enrolled in a course that I am no longer interested in taking. Can I get a refund?
L115: You may unenroll from ULCs at any time without impacting your academic record. If you unenroll within 10 calendar days of the course start date, you will automatically be issued a refund of the $25 enrollment fee. You may only receive one automatic refund per course. If you need to unenroll from a course a second time, please contact support at 【12†[email protected]】. Refunds will not be issued for the purchase of ASU credit.
L116: 
L117: Are these courses covered by military benefits?
L118: These courses are not currently covered by any military benefit.
L119: 
L120: Where can I get a 1098-T tax form?
L121: 
L122: You may request a 1098-T from Student Business Services via email at 【12†[email protected]】 or phone at 1(855)278-5080. Earned Admission learners cannot access 1098-T information from their 【10†My ASU†my.asu.edu】 page.
L123: 
L124: Can I use my employer’s “tuition reimbursement” towards Earned Admission?
L125: It depends on the employer. Some Earned Admission participants have successfully gotten their credits reimbursed by their company, so it won’t hurt to ask! It’s always best to talk with your HR department before you purchase your credits, and be sure to mention this is real college credit provided by Arizona State University.
L126: 
L127: What is the Starbucks Pathway to Admission?
L128: 
L129: You can learn more about the Starbucks College Achievement Plan and the Pathway to Admission 【16†here†starbucks.asu.edu】.
L130: 
L131: 【17†Image】
L132: ## College credit
L133: 
L134: How do these courses appear on my transcript?
L135: 
L136: These courses appear identically to a course you would take online or on campus as an enrolled ASU student. Once you complete a course and purchase the credits, they will immediately appear on your unofficial ASU transcript. Learn more about requesting an ASU transcript 【18†here†students.asu.edu】.
L137: 
L138: How long do I have to add a course to my transcript?
L139: You have one year from the date you complete your course to purchase credit. You can see the exact date on your learner dashboard next to the course button that says “Add to transcript.”
L140: 
L141: I’m not happy with the grade I earned in my course. Can I take it again?
L142: Yes! You may enroll in the course the next time it is offered. However, on-demand courses cannot be reset. You may take the course the next time it is offered in a session-based format or wait until a new version of the on-demand course opens on July 1, the beginning of ASU’s fiscal year.
L143: 
L144: How can I tell if I already have credit from another institution?
L145: If you have an application on file and transcripts were submitted, click on the transfer credit guide link in the Resources or Add Courses section of your learner dashboard to see what has transferred in. If you do not have an application on file, you will need to use the course search function of the 【19†Transfer Credit Guide†webapp4.asu.edu】 to find the course you took to determine if and how it might apply.
L146: 
L147: Can I take a course to replace a grade from another institution?
L148: No. If you have already completed a course, taking the same course with Earned Admission will not replace the grade you earned at another institution.
L149: 
L150: Can I use CLEP, AP, DANTES, or other national tests towards my Earned Admission requirements?
L151: 
L152: No. However, national tests may be used for college credit once you are admitted to the university. Learn more about how your test credits may transfer 【20†here†catalog.asu.edu】.
L153: How do my previous Universal Learner Courses align with the new ASU Gold Credit Designations?
L154: All ULCs that had a Maroon credit designation also have a Gold credit designation. That means courses you have taken previously with Earned Admission and ULC will still apply to ASU major maps. Courses can fulfill requirements in both General Studies Gold and General Studies Maroon. Incoming ASU students will be required to meet the 【21†General Studies Gold requirements†catalog.asu.edu】. More information about these changes can be found on the 【22†Provost general studies page†provost.asu.edu】.
L155: How soon can I get credit for an on-demand course?
L156: 
L157: 3 and 4 credit on-demand courses will become available to add to your transcript 6 weeks after enrollment. 2 credit courses can be added after 4 weeks and a 1 credit course can be added after 2 weeks.
L158: 
L159: During which session will an on-demand course appear on my transcript?
L160: An on-demand course will appear on your transcript in the session in which you complete the course. Course attendance dates will also be listed on your transcript. If your completion date falls near the end of a session, please contact our support team at 【23†[email protected]】 at least three weeks before the session ends and before adding the course to your transcript to confirm which session it will fall under. Once the course has been added to your transcript, the session cannot be changed.
L161: 
L162: 【24†Image】
L163: ## Degree programs
L164: 
L165: What is a Degree Pathway?
L166: 
L167: A low‑risk way to start ASU‑aligned courses in an interest area before formal admission. Degree Pathways allows a learner to select a degree program they are interested in and guides them on which ULCs will fit into that degree’s curriculum guide. Complete the pathway, then transition into your ASU degree.
L168: 
L169: What is the difference between Degree Pathways and Earned Admission?
L170: Degree Pathways is a way to guide your Earned Admission experience. All the same EA rules apply- you must complete 12 or 24 credits (depending on age) with a 2.75 GPA. However, some engineering programs have additional requirements like getting a 3.0 GPA or having a cumulative 3.0 GPA.
L171: 
L172: Does selecting a Degree Pathway mean I’m already enrolled in that degree program at ASU?
L173: No, Degree Pathways are designed to help track your progress toward a degree. You still have to apply to the university and select your desired program at ASU.
L174: 
L175: Does selecting an Engineering Pathway mean I’m automatically admitted to that program?
L176: No. Some Engineering Pathways have higher admission requirements, like having certain math or science competencies and a cumulative GPA of 3.0. Your cumulative GPA includes all previously transcripted course work from other institutions. If you have additional questions regarding a higher admission requirement Engineering Pathway, please contact our support team at 【12†[email protected]】.
L177: 
L178: What if I’m uncertain about what degree to pursue?
L179: If you’re currently unsure of your degree of interest, ASU offers the 【25†me3 career exploration tool†yourfuture.asu.edu】 to help you discover degree programs you may be interested in.
L180: 
L181: 【26†Image】
L182: ## Certificates
L183: 
L184: How do I get started?
L185: 
L186: It’s easy! Begin completing the courses listed on the specific certificate page. All certificate courses offer an on-demand option so you may begin at any time. Once you successfully complete and purchase all the courses required for a given certificate, you will receive an email containing your certificate with the ASU logo, your name and the name of the certificate you completed, along with transferable college credits.
L187: Do the courses I complete while pursuing an ASU certificate count towards earning my admission into ASU?
L188: 
L189: Yes, as long as you complete your required number of credit hours (either 12 or 24 depending on your age) with a 2.75 GPA or higher, you can use the courses in an ASU Certificate toward earning your admission. It’s a great way to get a credential that you can put on your resume while on your way to pursuing a bachelor’s degree.
L190: 
L191: How long does it take to earn an ASU certificate?
L192: Certificates consist of 3-6 courses, and learners typically take 1-2 classes at a time. The average completion time of each course is 8 weeks.
L193: 
L194: How do these courses appear on my transcript?
L195: 
L196: These courses appear identically to a course you would take online or on campus as an enrolled ASU student. Learn more about requesting a transcript 【27†here†registrar.asu.edu】.
L197: 
L198: Is there a minimum GPA requirement for earning an ASU Certificate?
L199: No, there is no minimum GPA requirement for certificates. However, If you’re using these courses to earn admission to ASU, you must pass each course with a C or better and have at least a 2.75 GPA to earn a certificate.
L200: 
L201: What happens if I enroll but don’t finish the requirements?
L202: While we hope everyone who enrolls will complete their certificate, there are no negative repercussions if you cannot finish the courses. Earned Admission offers the opportunity to try college courses with low cost and low risk. Keep in mind, if you are having challenges with the coursework, tutoring is available to ensure you successfully complete the program. Visit the 【9†ULC Online Study Hub†tutoring.asu.edu】 for academic support.
L203: Do I need to purchase all courses in the certificate to receive an ASU Certificate?
L204: 
L205: Yes, to receive an ASU Certificate, you must add all of the courses to your transcript by purchasing the credits before receiving the credential. However, you have up to one year after completing each course to pay the credit fee.
L206: 
L207: Do ASU Certificate courses go towards admission into ASU if I take them while attending high school?
L208: No, the courses will not count toward Earned Admission for high school students. However, it is a great way to get a credential that you can put on your resume while on your way to pursuing a bachelor’s degree.
L209:

L51: Information: After completing a Universal Learner course, you can choose to earn college credit that may be applied toward a degree program at ASU or transferred to another institution.   Steps to Receive Credit
L52:   1. Complete your course:  Finish your Universal Learner course with a final grade of C or better.
L53:   2. Pay the fee:  A new “Add to transcript” button will appear in your learner dashboard. Follow the steps and pay the $400 fee to add the course grade to your ASU transcript.
L54:   3. View your transcript:  Once processed, your credits will appear on your My ASU page and on your official ASU transcript.
L55:   Important Notes
L56:   * You have one year from your course completion date to add the course to your ASU transcript.
L57:   * Make sure you’re satisfied with your grade before paying, as you can only transcript a course once.
L58:   * If you’d like to retake a course for a better grade, you can do so the next time it’s offered.
L59:   Need Help?
L60:   * Support Coaches are available Monday through Friday, 7 a.m.–6 p.m. MST.
